title: The highest companion
hookLine: he dies resting on Aisha, saying, the highest companion (Bukhari)

lines: A HAND, A BREATH, A FEW WORDS.
cards: Today is a quiet day, and it should be. Some of you have sat with someone you loved as they died. You'll know the room goes very small.

The big things fall away, and what's left is a hand, a breath, a few words. It's the same Monday, later that day. The Prophet ﷺ is lying in Aisha's small room beside the mosque, his head resting on her.
She's the one who told what happened next, and Sahih al-Bukhari keeps her account, in its small, plain details.

teach.b: Her brother came in holding a siwak, the twig Arabs used to clean their teeth, and she saw the Prophet's eyes follow it.
She took it, softened the end with her own teeth, and gave it to him, and he cleaned his teeth with it.
There was a bowl of water beside him; he dipped his hands in it, wiped his face, and said: there is no god but God; truly, death has its pains.

teach.h: SHOWN HIS PLACE, THEN GIVEN THE CHOICE.
teach.b: And she remembered something he'd said while he was well: no prophet dies until he is shown his place in paradise and then given the choice.
Near the end, his eyes lifted, looking upward, and he said: Allahumma, ar-rafiq al-a'la. O God, the highest companion. And Aisha said: then I knew he would not choose us.

teach.h: RAFIQ — A COMPANION ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Rafiq means a companion, a friend on the road.

In another of Aisha's reports, he was heard in that illness saying the words of a verse in the fourth surah: with those whom God has favored, the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.
In Pickthall's translation, it ends: "The best of company are they!" So his last words weren't a command or a farewell speech. They were a choice of company.
Tradition places the day in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the eleventh year after the hijra. He died, she said, with his head resting between her chest and her neck. The room went very small.

how: Muslims send peace and blessings on the Prophet whenever his name is mentioned, and his death is remembered with deep love; at the bedside of the dying, families gently prompt the words there is no god but God, which he said in his last hours.

o: a companion, a friend on the road
an angel who guards the soul at night
a messenger who carries word from God

games.q: the small room — tap the pairs.
p: a twig for cleaning the teeth
then I knew he would not choose us

s: his last words were a long farewell speech
his last words were short: O God, the highest companion.
Aisha softened the siwak with her teeth for him
she saw his eyes follow it, and gave it to him.
he had said a prophet is given the choice before he dies
Aisha remembered it, and knew what his words meant.

games.q: the Prophet ﷺ has said no prophet dies until he is shown his place and given the choice. now his eyes lift upward. what does he say?
o: let me stay a little longer.
games.why: Allahumma, ar-rafiq al-a'la. and Aisha said: then I knew he would not choose us.

practice: Sit in silence today, or almost. If you've lost someone, let them be near you in the quiet; if you haven't, just sit with the story of the small room.
If you pray, you can send peace on the Prophet, as Muslims do when his name is said, or pray for the one you're remembering.

wordCard.voice: Rafiq. A companion, a friend on the road — the word the Prophet used for God in his last words, ar-rafiq al-a'la. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the highest companion. rafiq is a friend on the road; a'la means highest.

carryVoice: Your line: a choice of company. At the end of the road, he named his companion. Rest gently.
